articles.summary: Test duration is a property of the protocol, not the cell or the channel, which makes it hard to eyeball. Ionworks Operate predicts it by simulating the protocol, then schedules around real finish times.
articles.title: Predict how long a battery test will take

articles.summary: Most lab AI just summarizes a dashboard. The Ionworks Operate agent acts: it answers status in plain language, writes cycler protocols from a description, simulates them, and books them onto free channels.
articles.title: An AI agent that runs your battery test lab

articles.summary: Trying lab software usually means staring at a dead sandbox. So we built a live synthetic lab: sign up free, schedule a test, and watch it run, simulated in real time, on models that actually age.
articles.title: A synthetic battery lab you can drive, free

articles.summary: Most labs know what each cycler UI shows. Fewer can answer, in one place, what is running across Arbin, Maccor, Neware, and BioLogic right now. That gap is the real lab ops problem.
articles.title: What's running on your cyclers?

articles.summary: State of charge counts coulombs; runtime under a power load depends on energy. PyBaMM simulations of an NMC cell separate the two effects that make SoC overstate time to empty, and show why the gap grows with power.
articles.title: State of charge vs state of energy: why SoC overstates your runtime
